Incident reports and unusual consumption raise the planning floor, so a local surge is visible before shelves run empty.
Earliest-expiry-first simulation moves whole packs to hospitals that will actually use them before they expire.
Partners keep at least seven days of their own forecast demand, so helping a neighbour never creates a new shortage.
Each hospital's agent explains the evidence and negotiates counteroffers within strict, server-checked limits.
Every approval, reservation, pickup and receipt is recorded, and the evidence behind each decision can be exported.
Does Inception move stock on its own?
No. Inception proposes transfers, but stock is only reserved after both hospitals approve the exact terms. Agents can suggest counteroffers; they cannot approve or move stock.
Can a donor hospital run short by giving stock away?
Donors keep a protected reserve covering the longer of seven days or delivery lead time plus two days, and only hospitals with no projected shortage are asked to give.
Each forecast is checked against two simple baselines at past cutoffs, and the model with the lowest error is used. Uncertainty is always shown, not hidden.
What happens to stock that is about to expire?
Genuinely unused expiring stock triggers a search for a hospital that will consume it before expiry, so it is used rather than wasted.
